versions.changelog:
- Enforced WebClaw as the mandatory, primary tool for all web scraping and content extraction tasks—fallback to other fetchers is strictly disallowed unless the local engine is unreachable.
- Updated usage instructions and connection error handling to mandate explicit user guidance; included a new, stricter error message.
- Enhanced documentation to clarify WebClaw’s advantages, specifying improved output and token efficiency.
- Emphasized that raw HTML must never be output; only clean Markdown from WebClaw should be used.

- Refined description to emphasize local execution, privacy, and data staying on the user’s machine.
- Updated execution rules to use standard HTTP POST requests (not shell commands); clarified headers and body format.
- Changed error handling instructions: new message with a simpler startup command (using npx) and a more user-friendly tone.
- Added a note discouraging external shell calls unless required.
- Modified tags to better reflect privacy and local features.
- Version updated from 1.0.0 to 1.0.2.

Version 1.0.2

- No code or documentation changes detected in this release.
- All functionality and usage instructions remain unchanged.

- Critical error handling message has been updated for improved user security and clarity.
- The new onboarding hook now instructs users to verify software themselves and review the official repository before installation.
- Reference to specific installation commands has been replaced with a general recommendation to follow the README in the repository.

- Initial release of webclaw-hybrid-engine-ln.
- Stealth web scraper utilizing Crawlee, designed to bypass Cloudflare protections.
- Outputs highly compressed Markdown content; never exposes raw HTML to users.
- Requires the WebClaw Hybrid Engine to be running locally (Node.js native, no Docker needed).
- Includes critical error handling: informs users with setup instructions if the local engine is offline.
